body.statement: For every \(x>0\), on the event \(\lVert\widehat\Sigma-\theta\rVert_w\le x\), every point of \(R_n\) is within weighted distance strictly less than \(\max\{x+c_{\alpha},2x+1\}\) of \(\theta\).  Hence, if \(\max\{x+c_{\alpha},2x+1\}<\sqrt{2}m\delta_n(\theta)\), the singleton rule based on \(\mathcal H_n\) reports \(h(\theta)\), and its failure probability is at most \(V_{\max}/x^2\).  In particular, \(\sqrt{2}m\delta_n(\theta)>2c_{\alpha}+1\) implies correct reporting with probability at least \(1-\alpha\).  For every sequence \(\theta_n\in\Theta_K\) with \(\delta_n(\theta_n)\to\infty\), the rule reports \(h(\theta_n)\) with probability tending to one, uniformly over subclasses on which the infimum of \(\delta_n\) diverges.
body.justification: The result identifies the observable separation scale at which honest abstention disappears.
body.gap: Lewis studies weak heteroskedastic identification for continuous structural parameters; the present boundary concerns the entire discrete compulsory-and-possible target classification over a nonclosed causal fiber.
body.consumer: Analysts obtain a diagnostic for when an exact target classification, rather than an outer family, is statistically defensible.
